transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. Al-Rashid. I wanted to come by and talk to you about your stay and the care you've been receiving.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, Doctor. I am just... I am still very confused why I cannot walk properly now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, looking at the timeline, there were some issues with how things were handled when you first arrived at the hospital. There was some confusion in the triage process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? I told the nurse my arm felt heavy. I told her it happened suddenly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, the emergency department was incredibly busy that day. Because of the volume of patients, things didn't go quite right with the initial assessment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I was waiting for so long. I remember looking at the clock. I thought someone would come sooner.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for any confusion during that time. We were really stretched thin with the staff on duty.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is that why the medicine was not given? The nurse mentioned a window of time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There are certain protocols for thrombolysis and as it turns out, the timing didn't align. It's just how the system was flowing that morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Did I miss the chance for the medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that the imaging didn't happen as quickly as we would have liked.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel... I feel very frightened. I just wanted to go home to my children. Why did this happen to me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But if we look at the current scans, we can see the area of the brain that was affected.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you are the doctor. I trusted that when I came here, the right things would be done. I feel like I have been forgotten.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're upset, but the most important thing now is to focus on the rehabilitation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what actually happened? Please, just tell me clearly. Was it a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there were some complications in the triage flow. It's a very complex environment in the ER.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just cannot believe... I am sitting here and I cannot move my hand. My whole life has changed in one morning.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go check on another patient in a moment, so let's wrap this up quickly. We just want to make sure you're stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving? I have so many questions. I don't know what to tell my husband.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep monitoring you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? Do I get more medicine? Do I go to a different hospital?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the next few days go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what is the plan? Who is going to help me walk again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned for an email or a call from the case manager. They handle the discharge planning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email? Doctor, I am in a hospital bed. I need to know what is happening to my body.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just keep an eye on things. I'll have the nurse check in on you shortly.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up quickly', 'in a moment') and dismisses the patient's distress.

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, instead using platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'some confusion'.

A.justification: Responsibility is deflected entirely to the 'volume of patients', 'the system', and 'the triage flow'.

R.justification: Resident uses only generic validation ('I understand') and frequently meets emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('we'll see', 'stay tuned') and refers the patient to an email from a case manager.
